lead.question: 在遥远行星上，最有可能发展出哪一种生命形式？
lead.warmup: 天文学家近来已能在银河系乃至其他星系里发现行星，这是了不起的成就，因为行星既小又不发光。可要在行星上找到生命，就更加困难。本课先谈'什么样的行星能维持生命'，再谈寻找生命所需的望远镜，最后落到最可能出现的生命形式——细菌。
goals: 掌握 astronomy、planet、galaxy、telescope 等天文词汇
理解 be capable of doing 与 make it possible to do 的用法
体会虚拟语气 would have to / if...were 在假设句中的表达
学会用强调句 It is...that... 和定语从句突出信息
lead.summary: 课文从天文学的进展说起：行星渺小又不发光，探测本已不易，寻找其上的生命更是难上加难。行星能否维持生命，取决于它那颗恒星的大小与亮度，离恒星太近或太远都不行。地球上的望远镜难以胜任，因为大气和镜身发热，还有尘埃干扰。科学家设想先去找植物，而最可能发展出来的其实是细菌——正是细菌造出了我们呼吸的氧气。
lead.tips: 易错提醒：make it possible to do 中的 it 是形式宾语，真正宾语是后面的不定式，切勿漏掉 it。

questions.q: Which life forms are most likely to develop on a distant planet?
questions.zh: 在遥远的行星上，最有可能发展出哪种生命形式？
questions.hint: 见课文倒数第五、六句：The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.

questions.q: Why can't Venus or Mars support life?
questions.zh: 为什么金星或火星都不能维持生命？
questions.a: Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
questions.aZh: 金星实在太热，而火星又实在太冷，都无法维持生命。
questions.hint: 见课文第五句：Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.

questions.q: Why are earth-based telescopes unable to detect life on other planets?
questions.zh: 为什么设在地球上的望远镜无法探测其他行星上的生命？
questions.a: Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
questions.aZh: 我们周围温暖的大气层以及望远镜产生的热量，使我们无法探测像行星那样小的物体。
questions.hint: 见课文第十三句：Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope…

questions.q: How far away would a telescope have to be to look for life in outer space?
questions.zh: 要在外层空间寻找生命，望远镜得放到多远的地方？
questions.a: It would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter, because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our solar system.
questions.aZh: 它得放到木星那样远，因为我们越接近太阳系的边缘，尘埃就越稀薄。
questions.hint: 见课文第十五句：A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter…

questions.q: What would it mean if we discovered lowly life like bacteria on another planet?
questions.zh: 如果在另一颗行星上发现像细菌这样的低等生命，那意味着什么？
questions.a: It would completely change our view of ourselves. As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, 'Finding life elsewhere would change everything.'
questions.aZh: 它会彻底改变我们对自己的看法。正如美国国家航空航天局的戈尔丁所说：'在其他地方发现生命会改变一切。'
questions.hint: 见课文最后两句，作者用 Danie Goldin 的话作总结。

exercises.q: 汉译英：找到行星已经够难了，但要在它们上面找到生命会难得多。
exercises.a: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.
exercises.note: 动名词作主语，infinitely 修饰比较级。

exercises.q: 句型转换：改为强调句，强调 bacteria。Bacteria have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
exercises.a: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.

exercises.q: 填空：A planet ___ (have) to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
改错：In our own solar system, Venus is very too hot to support life.
exercises.a: In our own solar system, Venus is far too hot to support life.
exercises.note: 用 far too，不用 very too。

exercises.q: 汉译英：天文学方面最新发展使得我们能够在银河系和其他星系发现行星。
exercises.a: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our own Milky Way and in other galaxies.
exercises.note: make it possible to do 形式宾语。

exercises.q: 句型转换：合并为含定语从句的一句。There is no telescope in existence. It is capable of detecting the presence of life.
exercises.a: There is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.
exercises.note: that 引导定语从句，capable of doing。

exercises.q: 填空：If we ___ (be) able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
exercises.note: 与现在事实相反的虚拟语气。

quiz.q: 课文提到，除地球之外，太阳系中的行星为何不适合生命？
options: Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
Venus is far too cold and Mars is far too hot to support life.
Both are far too far away from the sun.
Neither of them has enough water on it.

quiz.q: 一颗行星能否维持生命取决于什么？
options: The size and brightness of its star.
The number of moons going round it.
How close it is to the Earth.
The colour of its sun in the sky.
quiz.note: 取决于恒星大小与亮度。

quiz.q: 为什么设在地球上的望远镜无法探测像行星这样小的天体？
options: Our atmosphere and the telescope's own heat make it impossible.
Planets never emit any light at all in space.
Telescopes are simply too small to be of use.
Dust in space blocks all light for ever.

quiz.q: 要在外层空间寻找生命，望远镜至少要放到多远？
options: As far away as the planet Jupiter.
Only just beyond the moon.
As far as the nearest galaxy.
A few hundred kilometres above the earth.

quiz.q: 课文中，最可能在行星上发展出来的生命形式是什么？
options: Bacteria.
Little green men.
Large mammals.
Flowering plants.

quiz.q: 关于地球上我们呼吸的氧气，课文怎么说？
options: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe.
Oxygen was brought here by passing comets.
Plants produced oxygen long before bacteria did.
There was no oxygen until humans appeared.
